symbols.name: ground-set size
symbols.meaning: The number of elements of the ground set $[h]$, which counts the elements the triples are drawn from.
symbols.quote: Let $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$ be the ground set, where $h$ is the number of its elements, and let $\mathcal T$ be the set of its three-element subsets.

symbols.name: triple family
symbols.meaning: The set of all three-element subsets of $[h]$.
symbols.quote: Let $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$ be the ground set, where $h$ is the number of its elements, and let $\mathcal T$ be the set of its three-element subsets.

symbols.name: triple
symbols.meaning: A three-element subset of $[h]$ in the family $\mathcal T$, used as an index of scalars.
symbols.quote: Let $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$ be the ground set, where $h$ is the number of its elements, and let $\mathcal T$ be the set of its three-element subsets.

symbols.name: triple
symbols.meaning: A three-element subset of $[h]$ in $\mathcal T$, which indexes one bank-X scalar and one bank-Y scalar.

symbols.name: bank X
symbols.meaning: The bank holding the bank-X scalars $x_S$, one for each triple $S$.
symbols.quote: Write $X$ and $Y$ for the two banks, which hold a scalar $x_S$ and a scalar $y_S$ for each triple $S$, and $x_T$ is the same family indexed by $T$.

symbols.name: bank Y
symbols.meaning: The bank holding the bank-Y scalars $y_S$, one for each triple $S$.
symbols.quote: Write $X$ and $Y$ for the two banks, which hold a scalar $x_S$ and a scalar $y_S$ for each triple $S$, and $x_T$ is the same family indexed by $T$.

symbols.name: bank-X scalar
symbols.meaning: The bank-X scalar held at triple $S$, on one wire.
symbols.quote: Write $X$ and $Y$ for the two banks, which hold a scalar $x_S$ and a scalar $y_S$ for each triple $S$, and $x_T$ is the same family indexed by $T$.

symbols.name: bank-Y scalar
symbols.meaning: The bank-Y scalar held at triple $S$, on one wire.
symbols.quote: Write $X$ and $Y$ for the two banks, which hold a scalar $x_S$ and a scalar $y_S$ for each triple $S$, and $x_T$ is the same family indexed by $T$.

symbols.name: side wire
symbols.meaning: The scratch wire for an ordered neighbouring pair $(S,T)$, which receives a copy of $x_T$.
symbols.quote: Scratch wires start with arbitrary values: $A_{ST}$ for each ordered neighbouring pair (the side wires), $C_i$ for each $i\in[h]$, and $C_\ast$ in the complex version.

symbols.name: central wire
symbols.meaning: The scratch wire for element $i$ of $[h]$, which gathers the $x_T$ over triples $T$ containing $i$.
symbols.quote: Scratch wires start with arbitrary values: $A_{ST}$ for each ordered neighbouring pair (the side wires), $C_i$ for each $i\in[h]$, and $C_\ast$ in the complex version.

symbols.name: total central wire
symbols.meaning: The extra scratch wire of the complex version, which gathers the sum of all $x_T$.
symbols.quote: Scratch wires start with arbitrary values: $A_{ST}$ for each ordered neighbouring pair (the side wires), $C_i$ for each $i\in[h]$, and $C_\ast$ in the complex version.

relations.quote: The subset-intersection finite network is built as a [linear network](linear-network.md) that swaps two banks of scalars indexed by three-element subsets, and [fast interchange of address chunks](tape-interchange.md) uses it for its scalar swap.
Complex version: scalars lie in $\mathbb Z[i,1/2]$, the set of [Gaussian dyadic numbers](gaussian-dyadic.md), and neighbours are distinct triples with even intersection.
